categories.name: Ambition
categories.description: An internal goal the character has set for themselves — love, status, power, wealth, spiritual knowledge. Ambition is about what this character wants to become or to get, and it is often self-interested. Decide the ultimate goal and how far they will go to reach it.

categories.name: Cause
categories.description: An external group or idea the character has committed to. It matters enough that they will take risks and work outside their comfort zone for it. A Cause is about who or what the character serves rather than what they want for themselves.

categories.name: Relationship
categories.description: A specific person, family, crew or people the character is bound to. What they do is driven by that bond — protecting it, honouring it, or getting back to it.

categories.name: Belief
categories.description: A principle the character holds about how the galaxy should work, and acts on. Belief is why they fight, as distinct from who they fight beside.

categories.name: Connections
categories.description: A tie to a person or group that pulls the character into the fight. They may never have wanted the war; they are in it because someone they are connected to is.

categories.name: Quest
categories.description: A goal the character is pursuing to its end — finding someone, recovering something, settling a score. The Quest is what gives the character somewhere to be going.

categories.name: Discovery
categories.description: Finding what has not been found — a world, a ruin, a species, the limits of a machine. For a character with this Motivation the journey to the discovery usually matters more than what anyone does with it afterward.

categories.name: Conflict
categories.description: The character is drawn to the fight itself rather than to what it achieves. Conflict covers the ones who seek it out — for mayhem, for conquest, for proving something.

categories.name: Creations
categories.description: Making something new and leaving it behind — a business, a work, a body of research, a settlement. The character wants to have built something.

categories.name: Faith
categories.description: Trust in something larger than the character — the Force, an order, a teaching. Faith is about what they hold to when holding to it costs them.

categories.name: Reward
categories.description: The character is in it to get paid. Reward covers the ones who take the risk for what it returns — credits, a ship, a debt cleared.

categories.name: Creed
categories.description: A single stated principle the character lives by and can say out loud. Where other Motivations stay vague, a Creed is concrete enough to be spoken — and a character may proclaim it under pressure or deliberately keep it to themselves.

categories.name: Oath
categories.description: A promise the character has made and holds themselves to. The Oath decides what they will and will not do, whatever the situation asks of them.

categories.name: Drive
categories.description: What pushes a character to lead. Drives cover the reasons someone takes responsibility for other people rather than only for themselves.

categories.name: Location: Aleen
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Aleen — fascination with the legends of the underground Kindalo, or a life changed by an encounter with the mystic Orphne. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Auratera
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Auratera — keeping the world unnoticed by the wider galaxy, or studying the archaeology gathered around its vergence. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Bardotta
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Bardotta — preserving its history against those who would sell it offworld, wandering under a vow of poverty, or quiet sympathy for the old Frangawl ways. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Devaron
categories.description: A Motivation rooted in Devaron and its matriarchal society, and the character's support for it. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Iktotch
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Iktotch — a sense of the future the character insists on acting upon, exile from the blockaded moon, or having collaborated with its occupation. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Lothal
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Lothal — climbing out of its poverty by any status symbol that will do it, or joining the revolt against the Imperial presence. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Naboo
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Naboo — mending the divide between the Naboo and the Gungans, carrying the galaxy's beauty home in word or song, or Gungan rights. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Ossus
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Ossus, for characters with ties to the world. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Location: Weik
categories.description: Motivations rooted in Weik — treating Force users as wizards to be revered, knowing one's place in its caste hierarchy, or seeing the wider galaxy as a sheltered wanderer does. Chosen rather than rolled: a character with ties to the world picks from the table instead of rolling a random Motivation.

categories.name: Innovation
categories.description: Building, improving and modifying. Innovation covers a Technician's reasons — fabrication, invention, refusing to let anything go to waste, plain fascination with how a thing works. The category was written for Technicians, and characters of other careers may take it at the GM's discretion.

categories.name: Pursuit
categories.description: A goal the character chases — wealth, happiness, vengeance, exploration. A Pursuit can run for a whole campaign, and can be about improving themselves as much as reaching the thing itself.

categories.name: Injustice
categories.description: A specific wrong done to a specific group. Narrower than a Cause: an Injustice always has identifiable people suffering it, and that is what the character acts against.

categories.name: Code
categories.description: Rules the character will not break, in a line of work that constantly invites breaking them. A Code covers the ones who work strictly to the law, or strictly to their own terms.

categories.name: Growth
categories.description: Improving oneself and others. Growth covers the ideals a Consular wants to spread — sometimes by saying them, more often by example.

categories.name: Improvements
categories.description: Making things work better. Improvements covers an Engineer's reasons — accuracy, efficiency, reliability — and the irritation of watching them done badly.

categories.name: Mysteries
categories.description: Questions the character needs answered — about the Force, about the past, about things the galaxy has forgotten. A Mystery keeps its hold for as long as it stays unsolved.

categories.name: Challenges
categories.description: Something the character has set themselves to overcome — an oppressor, an opponent, or a limit of their own. Challenges covers a Warrior's reasons for putting themselves in the way of it.

categories.name: Secrets
categories.description: What is hidden, and what the character does about it. Some are driven to uncover secrets, believing nothing should be kept from anyone; others work to keep them, believing the galaxy is sometimes better off not knowing.

specifics.name: The Dark Side of the Force

category_rolls.ten: roll once on each of any two categories
